messages:
maya: Quick check-in — I want to propose a smaller rollout metadata surface for pins. Current payload is noisy and we rarely use most fields. Thinking: a compact core + freeform annotations map. Anyone worried about losing important routing/affinity signals?
lucas: Curious, what's in your compact core? I'm worried about losing things we test for (eg. soft vs hard pinning semantics).
sophia: My take: keep explicit fields only for things that the runtime makes decisions on: phase (canary/stable/deprecated), affinity (hard/soft/none), priority weight, compatibility_hints (list). Everything else -> annotations. That keeps routing decisions deterministic. :+1:
kai: draft sketch: ```json
{
  "phase": "canary|stable|deprecated",
  "affinity": "hard|soft|none",
  "priority": "int(0-100)",
  "compatibility_hints": ["v1","v2"],
  "annotations": {"owner":"string","notes":"string", ...}
}
```
This is intentionally minimal. Runtime ignores unknown annotation keys.
jamie: Love the minimal approach. Operational questions: how do we version this schema? rollout manifests are long-lived in some tenants. We need a way to detect old clients that expect older semantics.
lucas: Right — suggest adding a small version field (semantic integer) at top-level, e.g., schema_version: "1". Also, keep a deprecation window policy in annotations so we can surface why a field was removed.
maya: Good call on schema_version. That avoids magic. Also want to capture an optional "fallback_variant" field that the router can use if the pinned variant is missing. That seems runtime-critical, not annotation.
sophia: Agreed — fallback_variant is used in routing/pathways. Add it to core but keep it optional. 
kai: Another trade: do we allow annotations to be typed (ints, strs) or just string blobs? Typed map is nicer but increases parsing complexity for languages. I'd prefer string-only values for annotations for portability.
jamie: String-only annotations + a well-documented annotation keyspace in the console should be fine. Ops can encode small JSON if needed (we already do that in some integrations).
deploy-bot: system: noticed rollout manifest v0.9 includes new schema_version key for tenant alpha-3. Will validate on next push.
lucas: Validation rules to add to validator: - schema_version required; - phase must be one of allowed enums; - affinity defaults to none if omitted; - annotations size cap (eg 4KB) to avoid explosion.
maya: Action items: 1) Kai — update runtime filter to read new core fields + fallback_variant, default affinity->none; 2) Lucas — produce a minimal validator and a migration playbook; 3) Sophia/Jamie — update Console doc pages + annotation keyspace guidance. I'll follow up with a short RFC note and example manifests. :eyes: 
sophia: SGTM. Also, we should run a small canary where older clients still send full payloads to ensure compatibility. If validator is strict we might reject older manifests, so validator should tolerate extra fields for at least one release.
maya: Agreed — tolerant by default, strict opt-in via validator flag. Thanks all — will post the follow-up RFC and a sample manifest in #architecture soon. :thumbsup:
